sdks.name: Bitmovin Player Android / Android TV / Android Fire TV

scopeNotes: The inventory retains the published Android configuration entries, public operations and reads, and named events. Nested configuration-owner entries are API paths, not a count of independent form fields. The original IDs, categories and exclusions remain unchanged.

SDK API settings provides typed values, lists, dictionaries, native object factories and editable callback bodies. The standard form remains available. Staged overrides take precedence after explicit Apply and player recreation; startup-only debug logging uses a saved next-process setting.

Commands invoke the current Player, Source, view or native host with edited arguments; reads refresh visible SDK state. Source identity and generation are checked for asynchronous results. Submitting a command does not establish its playback or service effect.

Named events have current-owner subscriptions and visible occurrence counts with SDK timestamps. Subscription wiring is not a record that every event fired; the matching source, feature, device or service is still required.

The app uses release 3.171.0 with the vendor +jason binary flavor required by IMA. The original standard source inventory is retained and compared with both published binary flavors. Only the explicit Media3 package relocation is normalized; standard source hashes are not presented as +jason binary hashes.

The 27 remaining configuration entries describe SDK-owned or internal metadata rather than supported independent inputs. They stay in the original denominator with a per-ID contract explanation. An unused constructed object or a read of SDK output does not become an editable setting.

These are source-level route mappings. Java virtual machine (JVM) unit tests, builds and representative licensed emulator checks are separate evidence. They do not qualify every argument combination, device, graphics driver, protected stream, Cast receiver or Analytics dashboard receipt.

scopeNotes: The inventory retains the original public Core API IDs, categories and exclusions. It covers configuration, SDK operations, state reads and typed event subscriptions; it is separate from the Analytics collector API.

Configuration drafts support typed values, arrays, native objects and edited callback bodies. Apply reloads the source or recreates the player. Parent configuration objects are credited only where an editable child reaches an actual SDK consumer.

The API inspector invokes typed SDK operations, displays current state and records named callbacks through listeners or Combine publishers. A returned value, accepted configuration or subscribed event does not qualify every media, operating system, device or remote service.

Native callback bodies use a JavaScript subset with CPU, elapsed-time, instruction and value-size limits. Generated Swift uses the same public bundled interpreter resources; those files and their license must be copied with the example.

The source DRM editor constructs FairPlay, ClearKey and receiver-side Widevine or PlayReady objects. The remote-source callback and receiver-conversion preview provide additional typed routes. Constructing a Widevine or PlayReady object does not add local Apple decoding support for that DRM system.

Original getter-only advertisement protocol members, SDK-internal ad lifecycle methods and system background-session callbacks retain individual limitations. They remain in the original denominator; no adjusted percentage is substituted for the reported coverage.

The app requires iOS 16 or later and uses Apple Player 3.128.0 with Google Cast 4.8.6. Cast initialization, receiver discovery and actual remote playback are different states; receiver playback requires a compatible device and service.

scopeNotes: The inventory covers the exported React Native wrapper configuration, Player and Source APIs, offline manager, Cast manager and named callbacks. It does not represent every API of the underlying native SDKs. Original IDs, categories and exclusions are retained.

Additional SDK configuration, collection editors and callback editors stage typed overrides. Explicit Apply recreates the player and reloads the source; source, player, view, Analytics and offline settings have separate consumers. A field supported on only one OS may have no effect on the other OS.

The API experiments panel runs the selected SDK method with edited arguments and displays its result and code. A void response establishes dispatch, not playback completion. Query the current SDK state and inspect the named events for the operation being tested.

Source changes retain creation identity until initialization settles and check ownership immediately before native attachment. A displayed operation timeout does not cancel an SDK call. Repeated requests keep one active initializer and the latest waiting request instead of accumulating native sources.

Cast receiver and namespace options are saved through the native startup adapter and take effect after the app process is fully restarted. Wrapper 1.29 initialize(options) is deprecated and does not apply those options. Startup values and native initialization do not establish receiver discovery, a connection or remote playback.

Named events have current-owner subscriptions and a bounded visible log. Editable callback bodies require explicit execution permission and run inside the app. Offline completion, advertising, protected media, casting and other services require matching inputs and environments; source-level routes are separate from those qualification tests.

The latest checked wrapper is 1.29.0, with its supported native dependency group: Apple Player 3.128.0 and Android Player 3.170.0+jason. The standalone Android sample uses 3.171.0+jason independently; changing only the wrapper native pin is not a verified wrapper upgrade.
